recognize_zh: 一顆顆粒球的細胞核呈完整的甜甜圈狀環形，中央包著一小塊細胞質「洞」，核染色質粗大並帶紫紅色顆粒——這就是環形核嗜中性球（ring neutrophil），在骨髓性腫瘤中常與 i(17q) 相關。
features: Granulocyte about twice the diameter of surrounding red cells
Nucleus forms a closed, doughnut-shaped ring enclosing a central island of cytoplasm
Coarse, clumped chromatin within the ring nucleus
Pinkish-grey cytoplasm with fine violet granules
Background normocytic, normochromic red cells and a single platelet
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a granulocyte with a ring-shaped (doughnut) nucleus enclosing a central clear zone of cytoplasm. The chromatin is coarsely clumped, and the cytoplasm contains fine granules. Surrounding red cells and the single platelet are unremarkable. Findings represent a ring neutrophil, a form of nuclear dysplasia that in a myeloid neoplasm such as acute myelomonocytic leukemia raises consideration of i(17q) or other cytogenetic abnormalities, but ring nuclei can also be seen in reactive and drug-related settings.

ddx.dx: Reactive or growth factor-associated ring nuclei
ddx.vs: Occasional ring-shaped band nuclei occur in reactive granulocytosis or G-CSF exposure, so significance depends on frequency and accompanying dysplasia.
A folded band has a U- or C-shaped nucleus with ends that overlap rather than a truly continuous ring with a central cytoplasmic hole.
Hypersegmented neutrophils have six or more discrete lobes joined by filaments rather than a single continuous annular nucleus.

ddx.dx: Monocyte with vacuolated or folded nucleus
ddx.vs: Monocytes have lacy chromatin, grey vacuolated cytoplasm and a folded nucleus without a sharply punched-out central ring.
